judged_text: The dialog re-declares ZAddGuestsInputSchema inline instead of importing the server's addGuests.schema.ts, and the two have already drifted: the client adds a uniqueness refine the server schema lacks. This is the classic parallel hand-maintained pair — the next validation change (e.g., a max-length cap on the server per the unbounded-array issue) will be applied to one copy and silently not the other, leaving client and server disagreeing about what input is accepted.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the client defines its own `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` (uniqueness) and uses it to validate `multiEmailValue` before calling `trpc.viewer.bookings.addGuests`. Separately, the server defines `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` as `{ bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email()) }` with no uniqueness rule. This is a diff-grounded, maintainability/consistency issue: client/server validation rules already differ and are maintained in parallel, which can lead to disagreements about accepted input as the API evolves (even if it doesn't currently prove a runtime failure from this diff alone).
